title: Residual lost-update window: a holder that was legitimately displaced (unverifiable owner stalled >30 s, or any holder stalled >1 h) and stalls after its last pre-rename check still renames over the displacer's acknowledged write
area: packages/core/src/job-queue/queue-store.ts saveQueue (token + content re-check, then rename) and queue-lock.ts judge
evidence: Pinned by test 'RESIDUAL, PINNED (ISS-JOBQSTALL-001)' in file-job-queue.stalled-holder.test.ts: B (wallNow = now + 1 h + 1 s) enqueues exactly at A's tmp->queue rename on the real fs; A ok, B ok, stored [fromA]. Not reachable for a live same-host holder below 1 h (the recorded ISS-JOBQLOST-003 reproduction, +31 s, now gives A ok / B conflict / stored [fromA]).
fix_direction: A rename cannot compare-and-swap. Closing it needs a primitive the queue does not have (e.g. a heartbeat that makes a live holder visible regardless of age, or a revision-checked store); until then keep critical sections short and wire callers to treat conflict as retry.
class: data write, narrowed to stalls >1 h (same host) or >30 s (unverifiable owner) between the last check and the rename; not closed

title: No defence against pid reuse or a dead worker thread: a lock whose owner died but whose pid is alive (reused pid, or a terminated thread of a live process) blocks every writer with conflict for up to 1 h
area: packages/core/src/job-queue/queue-lock.ts judge + defaultQueueIsAlive (liveness is pid-only, no start-time or heartbeat)
evidence: Real fs, checker-written test: (S4) lock body {pid: a live unrelated process, host: this host, at: now-10min}: enqueue with the default 2000 ms wait returns conflict after 2012 ms, then taken over only at +1 h+1 s. (S5) a worker thread blocked at the rename and then worker.terminate()d leaves its lock; its pid is this live process and its thread id differs, so a new writer gets conflict after 307 ms (lockWaitMs 300) at +0 and at +59 min 59 s, ok only at +1 h+1 s. The wait is bounded and typed (not a hang) and nothing is lost; the queue is unavailable to writers for up to 1 h. Same residual as run-state-lock.ts (documented there and in queue-lock.ts header (c)); not mitigated by any start-time token. Same-hostname containers sharing the directory see a live holder as ESRCH (dead) and displace it at once; the header scopes the lock to one host.
fix_direction: Record the process start time (or a heartbeat mtime refreshed by the holder) in the lock body and treat a mismatch / stale heartbeat as dead; before wiring either add that or make the caller treat conflict as a retry-with-alert and document the 1 h outage as accepted.
class: availability of data write path, no loss
